title: States skipped by moving the shorter wall
summary: Advancing the left shorter wall inward from cap[0, 7] to cap[1, 7] skips all six narrower states that keep index 0 on the left with right wall 6 down to 1.
context: Wall heights appear in the "Input wall heights" table below (zero-based indices). At initial endpoints [0, 7], heights are 3 and 4 with the left wall shorter, giving capacity min(3, 4) × 7 = 21.
Container capacity is cap[i, j] = min(ht[i], ht[j]) × (j - i), multiplying the shorter wall height by the index span.
description: On the top row, a rightward arrow labeled "Move the shorter wall" connects cap[0, 7] → cap[1, 7]. Below, a brace labeled "Skipped states" spans a two-row by three-column grid of thumbnails keeping i = 0 fixed and setting j = 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 from left to right across the two rows.

The two tables below give the input heights and the six skipped states. While the thumbnails print only symbolic names cap[i, j], wall heights, water heights, widths, and capacities in the table are computed from the input heights and capacity formula.

frames.title: All six narrower containers with the left wall fixed at i = 0 have capacity below 21
frames.explanation: Every skipped state has width strictly less than 7 and water height at most original left wall height 3, so all six capacities stay strictly below the already recorded 21 and skipping them cannot miss the optimal solution. At [0, 3], right wall height 2 is even shorter than left wall 3, lowering water height to 2 across width 3 for capacity 6; the other five states have water height 3.
